voice: Valory B – Conversational Girl-Next-Door with Relatable Vibe

lines.text: Nobody draws a hexagon by working out where the six corners go. You'd need trigonometry for that, and you'd hate it. So don't.
Put your finger on the paper. Draw a line — any length, say ten centimetres. Stop. Turn a little to the right. Draw another ten. Stop. Turn the same amount again.
Keep going. Same line, same turn. After six of them you'll find you're back where you started, pointing the way you started.
So there's only one real question left. How much do you turn each time?
And the answer is lovely. By the time you're home, you've turned all the way round exactly once. A full circle. Three hundred and sixty degrees — and that's true whatever shape you walked.
So you've got a full circle to share out between six equal turns. Three hundred and sixty, divided by six. Sixty degrees each.

Now look at what you've actually built. Change the six to eight and turn forty-five instead — that's an octagon. Change it to three and a hundred and twenty, and it's a triangle. Change it to thirty-six and ten degrees, and from a step back it's a circle.
You didn't learn to draw a hexagon. You learned to draw every regular shape there is.
